title: Rumberos and Afro-Cuban pride
summary: He names rumberos like Tanganito and Malanga as creative dancers, comparing them to Savoy dances in New York.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Now, Macho was a young kid, he went to school but he was concentrating on music. At that time, Macho, Were there any popular Afro-Cuban musicians that made Afro-Cubans feel very proud?
Oh, definitely. Tres Linda Cubanas, ah- ah- El Gallo Blanco de Maria, ah-- numerous of son montunos because that was the backbone of the thing; and then they start......
What about musicians or rumberos de la calle? Were there many?
Oh yeah! Tanganito, Malanga, Andrea Baro, Roncona; you name it.

Well, they was people like they was, let's say, they improvised. They was dancers, professional dancers in their own right; so they was so creative that in everyplace, because that was the only outlet we had, dance. Like when I came here I saw the Savoy, how many dances they create at the Savoy. Susie Q, Big Apple, Jitterbug, so forth, so on; so that's the only outlet we had in those years.
